title: Almanac pool
description: The published pool. Opinion free: no score, rank or affinity. Bodies live in bodies/<article_id>.json, never here (R12). Every object is closed, so an unknown field is a contract change, not a silent addition.

events.description: S31: the Live tab's event list (R22). Optional: added by S32 fanout runs, same as source_health; older pools predate it. The fetcher emits an empty array until S32 fills it.

utc_timestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, second precision, Z suffix.

id.description: Filename safe, so bodies/<id>.json is always a valid path.

https_url.description: S38: image urls are https only, stricter than http_url used for article and feed links (R34).

nullable_utc_timestamp.description: S06: same shape as utc_timestamp, or null before a source has ever reached that state.

country.description: DESIGN-bundles section 3 and 4: the outlet's home country, hand-entered, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Feeds section 4a's locality term. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it.

roster.description: DESIGN-bundles section 3: provenance only, why the source was added. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it.

paywall.description: DESIGN-bundles section 3 and 4a: hand-entered, true when the outlet meters or blocks its articles. Feeds section 4a's paywall term. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it.

exile_of.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4 and R42: for an exile newsroom, the country it reports for (distinct from country, where it is based), ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. The pair (outlet, exile_of) counts as intermediate. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it for any exile newsroom in sources.json.

topic.description: S08: closed tag set from topics.json. hard_news there names the R16 hard-news subset (world, politics, economy, science, conflict).

lean_bucket.description: S08: closed set from fetcher/taxonomy.py. Lean is a shared, repo-owned claim about a source (R10); trust is personal and lives on the device, never here.

country_code.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case. This checks the shape only (two upper-case letters), not membership in the real ISO list; a lowercase or three-letter code is rejected.

roster.description: DESIGN-bundles section 3: provenance only, why a source was added. Nothing reads it for ranking, leading or publishing (R40 answer 3).

locality_tier.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4, R40 answer 5, R42: local when the outlet's country is a story country; intermediate for a listed pair (HK or MO on CN, MY and SG on each other, or an exile newsroom's exile_of country); overseas otherwise, including Taiwan on China stories.

primary_source.description: DESIGN-bundles section 3 and B9: a plain link out to the trumpstruth.org archive, never an embed. Shape choice (B3): the design doc guarantees only an https archive URL ('at least an archive URL'); this object is additive like the rest of the contract, so B9 can add more facts to it later without breaking this shape.

topics.description: S08: every article the fanout pipeline publishes carries at least one tag; optional here only so the S01 single-feed fetcher's pool (which predates topics.json) stays valid.

geo.description: G1: where the story is, from the article's own title and dek (fetcher/geo.py, geo.json), never from its outlet. sg implies asia, asia implies world. Empty when the text names no place. Optional so pools from before G1 stay valid.

has_body.description: S22: true only when bodies/<id>.json was written this run (R12). Optional and false-by-omission so pools from before this slice stay valid; the reader (S25) treats a missing has_body the same as false.

countries.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4 (G1): ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries this article's own title and dek name, never the outlet. No cap here; section 4's at-most-2 cap is a property of a cluster's derived story_countries, not of one article's raw extraction. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it.

locality.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4: this version's tier against the story's country or countries, a fact computed in the cron. Omitted (no label) when the story has no country or more than 2. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it.

bv.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4a: best-version fact terms, fixed order (original, complete, depth, headline, locality, first, health, paywall; trust is added on the device, never here), one integer each, published only for stories with 2+ outlets. Shape choice (B3): the section 4a table lists 9 rows but says 'every term but trust is a fact... published per article as bv', so bv excludes trust, fixing the length at 8; values are left unbounded since per-term floors and caps are B8's to compute, not this contract's to police. Optional and additive (B3); B8 starts writing it.

watch.description: W2 (R50): the watch tags of the users' queries (followed phrases, standing-story keywords) whose Google News search found this article, or found a copy of it. A tag is 'w:' plus the first 10 hex characters of SHA-256 of the normalized query (trimmed, lowercased, spaces collapsed), so the pool never carries a query itself. Optional and additive: absent on every article no search found, and on every pool from before W2.

watch_tag.description: W2: 'w:' and 10 lowercase hex characters, the hashed form of one watch query.

article_image.description: S38: optional, stated by the feed itself, never fetched or probed (R34). Sourced in priority order from media:content, media:thumbnail, an enclosure with an image type, or, as a last resort, the first inside the item's own description or content:encoded. width and height are only present when the feed states them; credit is attribution or caption text the feed gives, also optional.

cluster.description: S07: one story, computed locally (R8). article_ids lists published members only; every article belongs to at most one cluster. method names how the members were linked: minhash for syndicated near-duplicate copies, cosine_entity for independently written coverage (TF-IDF cosine plus a shared key entity inside the time window), or both. near_duplicates groups the ids that are copies of one piece of copy, kept and marked rather than dropped, so a later slice can count independent sources (R16). S08: independent_sources counts distinct syndication groups among the cluster's sources, not distinct source_ids, so two outlets carrying the same wire copy count once (fixes the S07 deferral). lean_buckets is the set (no duplicates) of lean buckets those sources cover; R16 must-know eligibility needs at least two.

lean_buckets.description: W2: empty only when no member's outlet has a listed lean, which happens when every member came from fetcher.watch's Google News source (outlets sources.json does not list, so no lean is claimed for them). Such a cluster can never be must-know, which needs two.

story_countries.description: DESIGN-bundles section 4: countries named by at least half of the story's versions, at most 2 (bilateral stories such as US and CN), a fact computed in the cron and used to derive each version's locality. Shape choice (B3): section 4 states the at-most-2 cap directly; a zero-country story is unlabeled rather than an empty list, so minItems is 1 when the field is present at all. Optional and additive (B3); B4 starts writing it.

primary_source.description: DESIGN-bundles section 3 and B9: the trumpstruth.org archive link for a matched Truth Social quote. Optional and additive (B3); B9 starts writing it.

event.description: S31: one entry in the Live tab's event list (R22), computed in the cloud by S32. An event groups clusters sharing a key entity within 48 hours. cluster_ids names those clusters; every cluster belongs to at most one event, the same closed-shape rule as an article belonging to at most one cluster. hype is the R22 score, distinct clusters in the event times independent outlets covering it in the last 24h, so it is a non-negative count with no stated ceiling. eligible mirrors R16 must-know eligibility (hard news topic tags, independent sources spanning at least two lean buckets); live is the actual Live tab placement and can only be true when eligible is also true, since R22 says a celebrity story can never go live regardless of hype. hold_state is the R22 hysteresis bookkeeping across runs, an incumbent holds at least 12h even if it would no longer qualify on this run's numbers alone: none for an event that is not being held (never live, or currently live purely on its own merits), holding for one kept live past what eligible/hype alone would earn it this run, released for one that was held and whose hold period has since ended.

live_since.description: S32: when this event took the Live slot, present only while live is true. The 12h hold floor (R22) is measured from it, and it is the one piece of hysteresis state the previous pool must carry that the fields above cannot. Optional, so pools from before S32 stay valid.

drop_counts.description: S02: fixed reason keys, closed set. An unknown key is a contract change, not a silent addition.

feed_states.description: S05: every configured feed ends in exactly one state per run, closed set. Item-level drops (drop_counts) are separate from this feed-level outcome.

health_state.description: S06: same closed set as feed_states, one source's outcome this run.

source_health_entry.description: S06: one source's health, carried forward run to run. last_ok_at is the generated_at of the most recent run this source reached state ok; last_item_at is the newest published_at seen among that run's items, so a feed that answers ok with stale copy is visible even though last_ok_at keeps advancing. consecutive_empty and consecutive_error each count the current unbroken run of that outcome, ending at this run, and reset to 0 the moment a run does not match. items_fetched is this run's raw item count (0 unless state is ok). unhealthy is set once consecutive_error reaches 3 or consecutive_empty reaches 5 (fetcher/health.py).

source_health_map.description: S06: per-source health keyed by source id. Optional: added by S05 fanout runs, same as feed_states; the S01 single-feed fetcher's pool predates it.

image_found_counts.description: S38: closed set of extraction methods, each mapped to how many published articles got their image that way.

image_rejected_counts.description: S38: closed set of rejection reasons, each mapped to how many candidate images were discarded that way. not_https and data_uri are unusable urls; tiny_pixel is a 1x1 or near-1x1 stated size, a tracking pixel not content; repeated_placeholder is a source giving the exact same image url on every one of its own published items, a logo, not a photo.

image_counts.description: S38: per-run image outcomes, added by S05 fanout runs only (the S01 single-feed fetcher predates it, same as feed_states).

counts.description: Run ledger. drops maps a fixed reason key to count (S02); leniency maps each parser tolerance applied (R9) to count, keys open. feed_states is optional, added by S05 fanout runs: it maps each closed feed-level outcome to a count, and the sum equals the number of configured sources. fetched == published + sum(drops) is asserted on every run. previous_pool_status is optional, added by S06: it records where this run's carried-forward state (source health, event holds) came from: cache (F6, the actions/cache-restored state.json, read before any network call), ok (the live pool.json read succeeded), absent, unreachable, or old_schema (predated this slice's schema, or was not a valid pool, e.g. an Access login page). images is optional, added by S38: found and rejected are closed-set maps of image outcomes for the run. bodies is optional, added by S22: written/skipped/bytes for this run's bodies/<id>.json output. routes is optional, added by F3: how many configured sources are wired to each fetch route (direct, relay, google_news), regardless of whether the run's fetch succeeded. watch is optional, added by W2 (R50): the run's watch searches (watch_counts); its candidates are part of fetched.

watch_counts.description: W2 (R50): this run's watch searches, counts only (the queries themselves never leave the fetcher). kv is how the Workers KV read went: ok, no_token (no token or account id in the job's env), no_namespace (almanac-interests does not exist), http_<code> (403 is a token without Workers KV Storage Read), timeout, network, bad_response or error. queries is how many were searched after query_drops. fetched is the raw items across every search feed; each ends as a candidate or in drops, so fetched equals candidates plus the sum of drops. A candidate the pool already had is merged (its tag added to that article); the rest, with pool articles a tag saves from the per-source cap, publish exempt from that cap while bytes (their records, plus the tags on articles that publish anyway) fit budget_bytes; published and over_budget count them. errors counts failed searches by status (http_<code>, timeout, network, too_large, parse_error, error). The main ledger sees each candidate once: merged ones as duplicate_url, over-budget ones as over_cap.

query_drops.description: Queries not searched, by reason: bad_value (a KV value unreadable or not v1), bad_query (no q, an empty q or one over 100 characters), bad_tag (the tag is not the hash of its q), over_value_cap (past 25 in one value), duplicate (the same tag again), over_cap (past 60 for the run).

drops.description: Search items dropped before they became candidates: the S02 item checks (no_title, bad_url, no_date), stale (older than 3 days), over_query_cap (past a query's newest 10), duplicate (the same article from another query, whose tag it joins).

body_counts.description: S22: this run's bodies/<id>.json outcomes. written is how many files were written. skipped_teaser is published articles from a full_text_ok source whose feed item did not itself clear the full-text length test live (a teaser, not a body). skipped_cap is candidates that cleared the test but were skipped because MAX_TOTAL_BODY_BYTES for the run was already spent. bytes is the total size of the files actually written.
